name: Electroreception Lateral Line
description: Introduces shark-derived ampullae of Lorenzini — specialized electroreceptor organs — along the jawline, temples, and forearms. The user gains the ability to detect bioelectric fields generated by living organisms and active electronics within a 3–5 meter range. The sensation is described as a 'pressure' or 'tickle' that varies with the strength and frequency of the field. Living bodies produce distinct signatures; electronic devices produce others. A skilled user can detect a person hiding behind a wall by their bioelectric field, identify the type of electronics someone is carrying, and sense the presence of active surveillance equipment. Gravemoss Biofoundry developed the modification for security applications, but it has found a wider market among the paranoid, the curious, and the professionally cautious.
source_organism: Carcharodon carcharias (great white shark), Ornithorhynchus anatinus (platypus, terrestrial electroreception)
procedure: Subdermal implantation of electroreceptor organ buds with neural integration, 3 sessions
side_effects: Overwhelming input near heavy electrical infrastructure
Ampullae visible as small dots along jawline and temples
Rare: phantom field sensations in electrically quiet environments
social_perception: Professional and paranoid-adjacent. Shark Sense users are either security professionals or people who live in environments where knowing what's behind the wall matters. The visible ampullae dots are recognizable to those who know what they're looking at.
story_hooks: A Shark Sense user detects a bioelectric field with no source — something is generating a living signature inside a wall, and it's been there for months
An electroreception user discovers they can detect the specific bioelectric signature of a particular geneware modification, allowing them to identify modified individuals by their electrical output
